summary.headline: Anand Rathi Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 125.7% YoY to ₹416 million on revenue of ₹2,557 million, while the MTF book fell 10.53% QoQ.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 28.1% YoY to ₹2,557 million, with EBITDA up 51.4% to ₹1,103 million (43.2% margin) and PAT up 125.7% to ₹416 million. Full-year FY26 revenue grew 10.2% to ₹9,322 million, EBITDA rose 21.9% to ₹3,796 million, and PAT rose 24.8% to ₹1,293 million. Non-broking income (MTF interest, distribution, other) rose to 53% of the mix in Q4 and 49% for the year, while the MTF book declined from ₹12,317 million in December 2025 to ₹11,019 million in March 2026 due to RBI funding-policy changes and weak markets. Management proposed a ₹5 per share dividend.

segments.name: Broking and related services
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue ₹1,201 million (+14.5% YoY); FY26 ₹4,755 million (-6.8% YoY). FY26 mix: equity cash 51%, F&O 41%, other 8%; Q4 mix: 49%, 41%, 10%.

segments.name: Non-broking (MTF, distribution, other)
segments.commentary: MTF book ₹11,019 million with zero NPA and ~61% of exposure from clients with balances below ₹1 crore. Distribution income rose 44.1% in FY26 to ₹1,129 million, spanning MF, PMS, AIF, insurance, bonds, structured products and FDs.

segments.name: Asset management / custody
segments.commentary: AUM ₹77,876 million (+21% YoY); assets under custody ₹944,155 million (+16% YoY). Insurance corporate agency licence obtained in FY26; life and health insurance distribution has started.

guidance_outlook: Target revenue mix of 50:50 between broking and non-broking, with both growing steadily; management said it is not yet happy with the current 51:49 split and expects to reach 50:50 over time.
Management expects non-broking to grow about 40-45% annually for the first few years, and broking about 15% a year.
Overall revenue growth aim of about 15-20% YoY.
Earlier guidance of an MTF book of ₹15,000 million by FY26 was missed; the book ended at ₹11,019 million.
Debt-equity ceiling set at a maximum of 1.5x; current ratio is about 0.6x.
capex_capacity: MTF book contracted 10.53% QoQ in Q4 FY26 after RBI policy changes narrowed bank and NBFC funding avenues for capital market intermediaries; management said the company had to control growth and preserve cash for margin requirements.
Management said the RBI funding-related deferral was postponed to another quarter, and expects to resume MTF growth as funding routes reopen.
IPO completed in September 2025 raising ₹745 crore, used mainly for working capital.
Stock basket for MTF restricted internally to fewer than 1,000 stocks versus about 2,000+ permitted by the regulator; internal margins set above exchange margins for many stocks.
Branch network and business partner expansion planned in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.
demand_pricing: Market backdrop: Nifty fell about 15% in Q4 FY26 and the company described a consolidation phase, FII outflows and West Asia-related volatility; clients became cautious on new and existing positions.
Demat accounts rose from 15.14 crore (Mar 2024) to 22.2 crore (Feb 2026); mutual fund AUM about ₹82.02 lakh crore (Feb 2026), up 24.8% YoY.
Active client base was flat to down 2-3% in FY26, while total client base grew 12.7% (corrected from 12%).
MTF yields: management said no significant pricing pressure yet despite competitor entry, with low MTF penetration among its clients; it did not rule out yield changes.
About 42% of active clients have been with the company for over five years; 83% of active clients are over 30 years old; about 60% of broking clients use the digital platform.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company guide broking and wealth management over coming quarters (client acquisition, advisory, digital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wealth management sits in a separate group company; this entity focuses on broking and distribution, with a phygital model and about 60% of broking clients on the digital platform.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage risks in broking and advisory (volatility, compliance, credit) while keeping profitability stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited restricting the MTF basket to under 1,000 stocks, higher-than-exchange margins, zero MTF NPA over eight-plus years, QSB broker status and a debt-equity ceiling of 1.5x.

qa_highlights.question: How should the 50:50 broking/non-broking mix evolve over the next couple of years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects non-broking to grow 40-45% a year and broking about 15%, with overall revenue growth of 15-20% a year.

qa_highlights.question: Are MTF spreads sustainable amid new competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not facing much pressure yet due to pent-up demand and low utilisation; yields may change but it aims to maintain current levels, with growth gated by capital and funding.

qa_highlights.question: How much of broking is derivatives vs cash, and what is the STT impact? What is exposure to the RBI proprietary-trading rule?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue split is about 50:50 cash vs derivatives, with focus on hedged and investment-led F&O and commodity trades. The company said it has no proprietary book, so the RBI prop-book rule does not affect it. The STT impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How much of AUC growth came from new clients vs existing clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AUC growth came mainly from existing clients, with the total client base up 12.7% and active clients flat to down 2-3% in FY26.

risks_watch: MTF book contraction (down 10.53% QoQ) and dependence on bank/NBFC funding under RBI rules; watch the funding reopening and the ₹15,000 million target.
Broking revenue fell 6.8% in FY26 with active clients flat to down, and F&O is 41% of the mix; the sensitivity to market cycles and STT changes is not quantified.
Competition in MTF could pressure yields; management said it is not yet seeing it.
Q4 PAT (+125.7%) may not be a clean run-rate given the quarterly volatility; watch whether margins hold when markets are weak.
Growth in non-broking (40-45%) and broking (~15%) is aspirational, given FY26 broking was down.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, distribution and asset quality (zero MTF NPA), but cautious on market conditions and the MTF book, which management attributed to RBI funding changes and client caution. Answers on STT, yields and derivatives mix were generalised with few figures.
key_quotes: As of March 31st, 2026, our total assets under custody stood at approximately ₹ 944,155 million, representing a growth of about 16% year-on-year.
we closed the year with zero NPA in the portfolio, reflecting our continuous underwriting standards and strong focus on asset quality.
we do not deal with proprietary book. We do not have a single pie on a proprietary activity in this book.

financial_highlights.change: +61% YoY; -10.53% QoQ from ₹12,317 million in Dec 2025

adds.what: Branch network and business partner expansion in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets (no count given)

growth.why: Management aims for 15-20% YoY revenue growth, with non-broking at 40-45% and broking at about 15%, but backing is vague: no specific capacity or order numbers, and the MTF book fell 10.53% QoQ and missed its ₹15,000m FY26 target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was 43.2% and FY26 was 40.7%, but Q4 PAT jump (+125.7%) may not be a clean run-rate, and management did not guide margins; broking is market-linked and STT impact was not quantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network and business partner expansion in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets is planned with no count or capex given; MTF growth is gated by funding, so capacity-led growth is not firmly dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides non-broking growth of 40-45% a year and broking around 15%, but MTF book fell 10.53% QoQ to ₹11,019m and FY26 broking revenue was down 6.8%, so near-term volume growth is uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The ₹15,000m MTF target for FY26 was missed (book at ₹11,019m) and the MTF book contracted in Q4, so no upgrade is indicated.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Aspirational 40-45% non-broking and 15% broking growth looks stretched given the MTF contraction, RBI funding constraints, and FY26 broking decline of 6.8%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Life and health insurance distribution started after the FY26 corporate agency licence, and broader distribution spans MF, PMS, AIF, insurance, bonds, structured products; no specific new product launch dated.

rows.label: MTF book recovery as funding reopens
rows.why: Management expects to resume MTF growth as funding routes reopen, but the book fell from ₹12,317m (Dec 2025) to ₹11,019m (Mar 2026), a 10.53% QoQ drop, and the ₹15,000m FY26 target was missed.

rows.label: Balance sheet deleveraged
rows.why: Debt-equity ratio fell to 0.62 at 31 Mar 2026 from 1.8 a year earlier, well inside the 1.5x ceiling, after the ₹745 crore IPO in September 2025.

rows.label: MTF yield pressure from competitors
rows.why: Management sees no significant pricing pressure yet due to low MTF penetration, but did not rule out yield changes as competitors enter.

tone.note: Management was confident on distribution growth, zero MTF NPA and the balance sheet, but cautious on the MTF book contraction and market conditions; analysts pressed on STT, derivatives mix and MTF yields, and answers were generalised with few figures.
